items.title: Saints in the Wethouse
items.note: The Lancashire artist's debut album, out Nov 13 on XL. Pitchfork hears heavy noise-rap with overwhelming bass, and the review's headline points to a turn from harsh noise toward ambient tenderness.

items.title: Love's Arp
items.note: His fourth album, out Nov 6 on True Panther. Pitchfork calls it muted experimental R&B, a tribute to a romance and to Black music history. Clash mentions East African rhythms, vintage gospel and house-inspired sound design.

items.title: Advanced White Trash
items.note: The LA saxophonist steps away from jazz here. Pitchfork describes Auto-Tuned vocals, hip-hop beats and fantasy themes, so expect something odd.

items.title: Music for Empty Stadiums
items.note: John Talabot's first solo full-length in over a decade, 95 minutes long on AD 93. He started it in lockdown, and Philip Sherburne's review hears dancefloor tracks built on sharp supersaws and cycling arpeggios.

items.title: SWALLOW!
items.note: Pitchfork 7.2. Her second album leans on trip-hop and big beat, and the review says the bonkers electronics are the best bits.

items.title: Texture Songs
items.note: Solo guitar and voice on Bill Orcutt's Palilalia label. Pitchfork notes extended guitar techniques and free-improv energy under quiet, understated singing.

items.title: Rapid Response EP
items.note: A 12-inch of three long pieces. Pitchfork hears him going further into dark new age psychedelia.

items.title: valley and structure
items.note: Pitchfork 7.4, the best score in this batch. A Thrill Jockey album that follows sentence structure in the country, the record Pitchfork says started a new stage for Rubio.

items.title: Quiet Forest
items.note: A reissue of his 1996 album, the last full-length released in his lifetime, inspired by a visit to the Hoh Rainforest. Pitchfork says it shows a playful side, and the new CD came out Nov 13 with vinyl due in December.

items.title: RUIN: It's Not Just Music
items.note: Pitchfork 6.4, so a mixed review that compares it with out-there records like Gush and The Kid. It is the first release on her own label, Someone Special.
